newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-RAIN POSTPONES GRAND SLAM OF GOLF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RAIN POSTPONES GRAND SLAM OF GOLF.

text.p: Tuesday's scheduled opening round of the MasterCard PGA Grand Slam of Golf was washed out by heavy rain which flooded bunkers and saturated the Poipu Bay Resort golf course.
The two-day, 36-hole event features an elite field of this year's four major championship winners -- Nick Faldo (Masters), Steve Jones (U.S. Open), Tom Lehman (British Open) and Mark Brooks (PGA).

"Our plan right now is to begin Wednesday and get in as many holes as possible," said Julius Mason, spokesman for the PGA of America. "If we have to use Thursday to finish, we will. Our goal is still to play a 36-hole event."

The heavy rain and wind gusts up to 40 mph (65 kph) flooded many of the small two-lane roads on the small Hawaiian island of Kauai and produced high surf along its coastline. One beach house on the northern shore was swept out to sea.
The weather forecast called for more rain Wednesday morning before clearing skies in the afternoon.
